phase: protocol fixed before new implementation/selection outcomes
scope: Retrospective development evaluation on previously inspected 26 tasks. Fresh implementation, jobs and outputs; old R6-R8 artifacts are excluded as experiment inputs.
aggregation: Maximum valid win fraction; ties prefer more valid unique comparisons, remaining ties retained and evaluated as uniform selection. Fresh implementation.
active_query: After a shared random-chain spanning tree, choose the unseen edge whose two hypothetical valid outcomes most change the final uniform top-set distribution (total variation). Tie: touches current top, smaller observed degree sum, seeded random tie order. A heuristic, not a calibrated posterior or regret guarantee.
pool_admission: Finite candidate scores; one lexicographic representative per exact code hash; require complete raw-feedback coverage within each pool. Selection uses identity/coverage only, never utility rank. Report exclusions and conditional scope.
budgets: At most 13 unique source feedback reads per method/job, or complete pair count for small pools; cache rereads and budget-denied requests separate. Same feedback bank and cost cap, original tournament may spend fewer calls.
prediction: Decision-sensitive allocation reduces regret vs corrected original; coverage-random controls separate coverage from active allocation. Failed hypotheses are reported without retuning this run.
decision_rule: Report paired task-cluster 95% intervals plus per-task effects; both main and mechanism contrasts must be examined. No new-task or end-to-end improvement claim from this development replay.

resources.candidate_smoke_training: CPU, 3 archived models x 2 seeds, about 5 train seconds each, separate diagnostic adaptation

protection: Original source, baseline outputs and all R6-R8 artifacts remain unchanged. Corrected-source overlays and new policies have separate files and hashes.
preflight_amendment: If no complete pool at K is found in the prespecified 4000 label-blind coverage samples, try K-1, down to 2. All methods share admitted pools. Input-availability change before comparative outcomes.
